card.hook: Walk right up to Ljubljana Castle and you'll hit a funny problem: the hill and walls are far too big for your phone screen. The trick is to step back and let the Old Town do some of the work.
card.stand_here: Stand on Gallusovo nabrežje, on the opposite bank of the Ljubljanica from the castle side. Face east across the water, so the riverside Old Town facades fill the foreground and the castle rises on its hill behind them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the facades and the castle hill in one frame. If your phone has zoom 2x, try it to bring the castle closer so the hill doesn't look tiny. Skip 0.5x unless you want lots of foreground, because it shrinks the castle.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the facades along the lower third and the castle on the upper third, and keep your phone level so the buildings don't lean.
card.best_time: You're looking east, so afternoon light may be behind you and fall on the facades and the castle. Morning light may come from behind the castle and make it look darker. Check the light on the day.
card.selfie_here: Try the stairs down to the Ribja brv footbridge, between the Triple Bridge and Cobbler's Bridge, where you get a good view over the castle. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and tilt so the castle peeks over your shoulder. It's approximate, so check the screen before you tap.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the embankment across the river from the Gallusovo nabrežje facades, and pose with the castle in the background.
card.rules_and_safety: Gallusovo nabrežje is a public street, free to stand on. Check the riverside for people and bicycles before you shoot, and check the castle's official site before you go up.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the castle sits on the top third and not a single bicycle sneaks into the bottom. Bonus points for a smug face when you nail it.
card.good_to_know: The castle was probably built in the 11th century as a medieval fortress and rebuilt in the 12th. It got its present outline in a near-complete overhaul in the 15th century, and most of the buildings you see date from the 16th and 17th centuries. It was a prison in the 19th century, and today it's a major cultural venue. A funicular has run up the hill since 2006.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Gallusovo nabrežje, on the opposite bank of the Ljubljanica from the castle side. Face east across the water, so the riverside Old Town facades fill the foreground and the castle rises on its hill behind them.

card.hook: Picture a wide, tree-lined path with a cream-coloured mansion waiting at the far end and a row of lampposts leading you there. That's the Tivoli shot, and it's almost too easy.
card.stand_here: Stand in Jakopičevo sprehajališče, at the entrance end, and face east toward Tivoli Mansion. Centre yourself on the middle of the path so the trees and lampposts balance on both sides.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the straight view down the promenade. Try 0.5x to get more of the tree canopy, or 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to bring the mansion closer and make the lampposts look packed together.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and keep the mansion near the vertical centre line so everything looks tidy and balanced.
card.best_time: At the pond, guides recommend sunrise as a good time. The avenue itself is free and open at all hours.
card.selfie_here: Head to the castle gates and stand next to one of the four cast-iron dogs, so the mansion sits right behind you. Use the front camera and zoom 0.5x so the building fits over your shoulder. For a calmer selfie, try the bank of the fish pond with the old boathouse, Čolnarna, behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the lower end of the Jakopič Promenade and aim up the wide path, while you stand on the path so the whole mansion sits at the far end of the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: The promenade is a public park path, free and open at all hours. If you want to visit the mansion or other buildings in the park, check the official site first.
card.challenge: Photo panels often line the path, so try to find one and use it as a foreground frame, or step to one side and sneak a clean shot past it.
card.good_to_know: The park was laid out in 1813 to plans by the engineer Jean Blanchard. Jože Plečnik designed the promenade when he renovated the park in the 1920s. The mansion dates from the 17th century and got its neoclassical look in the middle of the 19th.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Jakopičevo sprehajališče, at the entrance end, and face east toward Tivoli Mansion. Centre yourself on the middle of the path so the trees and lampposts balance on both sides.

card.hook: Most bridges are happy with one span. This one has three, fanned out like a gentle funnel, and the pink church next door wants to be in your photo too.
card.stand_here: Stand in Prešernov trg, near the Prešeren statue, and face east toward the bridge. You'll see the three spans fanning out over the river, with the pink Franciscan church and the market colonnade in the frame.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the bridge and church. If you can't fit all three spans, switch to zoom 0.5x. Use zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for close-ups of the railings and the lamps.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and keep the phone level so the railings don't lean, then put the central span a little off-centre and let the church fill one side.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, when the square is nearly empty. Midday and December are the busy times.
card.selfie_here: Take it in Prešeren Square, beside the Prešeren statue. Use the front camera and turn so the bridge and the pink Franciscan church sit behind your shoulder. For a low-angle twist, step down to the riverside terrace below the bridge and let the arches rise above you.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by on Butchers' Bridge (Mesarski most), the glass-panelled footbridge just south of the Triple Bridge where the love locks are, and ask them to frame you with all three spans behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The bridge is in a pedestrian-only zone, so you'll walk the last stretch. It's free to visit at all hours.
card.challenge: Get all three spans in one shot with the railings perfectly straight. There are 642 balusters in the balustrades, so we won't make you count them.
card.good_to_know: A wooden bridge is mentioned here from 1280, and this is the oldest bridge in Ljubljana. The central stone bridge dates from 1842, and in the early 1930s architect Jože Plečnik added a footbridge on each side. The bridge has been part of UNESCO World Heritage since 2021.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Prešernov trg, near the Prešeren statue, and face east toward the bridge. You'll see the three spans fanning out over the river, with the pink Franciscan church and the market colonnade in the frame.

card.hook: Four big copper dragons crouch at the corners of a bridge in the middle of Ljubljana, and the cars driving past don't even look up. You'll be the one stopping to stare, and that's fine.
card.stand_here: Stand on Mesarski most, on the upstream (south) side, and look north toward the Dragon Bridge. You'll see all four dragons, with the market stalls and arcades in front of them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole bridge and all four dragons in one frame. Use zoom 0.5x only if you step right up to a dragon. For the tight shot from Resljeva cesta, try zoom 2x to 5x, depending on your phone, to squeeze a dragon, the cathedral towers and a lamp post together.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the arch along the lower third, and tap the bridge, then slide it a little darker if the sky behind it is bright so the dragons keep their detail.
card.best_time: Sunrise and early morning are the suggestion for this view, because the sun can rise behind the bridge. One guide prefers the west bank for afternoon and dusk light, so check where the sun will be when you visit.
card.selfie_here: Go to the Dragon Bridge pavement and stand right beside one of the four copper dragons on its pedestal. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x, and keep the dragon close in the foreground so the city sits behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on Butchers' Bridge, or on the market-side embankment just downstream of it, and frame you with the whole Dragon Bridge in view.
card.rules_and_safety: Personal photography is generally fine here, but commercial photography or filming may need permits. Watch for passing cars, because the pavements sit right beside the road, and stay out of the roadway.
card.challenge: Give each of the four dragons its own photo, then pick your favourite. Which one has the most attitude?
card.good_to_know: The bridge opened in 1901 and was built in the Vienna Secession style. It was one of Europe's earliest reinforced concrete bridges and the first of its kind in Ljubljana. It was first named after Emperor Franz Josef I and became the Dragon Bridge in 1919.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Mesarski most, on the upstream (south) side, and look north toward the Dragon Bridge. You'll see all four dragons, with the market stalls and arcades in front of them.

card.hook: Picture a bronze poet and his muse standing in front of a big pink church, and you get the postcard everyone in Ljubljana takes. You get it from the Triple Bridge.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje) and face back toward Prešeren Square. The statue of France Prešeren sits in the middle distance, with the pink Franciscan Church filling the background.
card.zoom: Zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to bring the church facade up close behind the statue. Zoom 1x gives you a wider scene with more of the square. Save 0.5x for when you're down in the square and want everything in one frame.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the statue on one of the vertical lines, then tap the statue and drag the brightness slider a touch darker so the pink church and the sky keep their colour.
card.best_time: Golden hour, around sunset, is the time several guides recommend for this view. Around the festive season a Christmas tree and event stages can block the view, so have a look before you settle on a spot.
card.selfie_here: Stand in the square beside the Prešeren statue, switch to the front camera and keep the pink Franciscan Church behind you. A travel guide says the square works well for selfies, and the statue and church make a backdrop that's easy to recognise.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Triple Bridge looking back toward the square, while you stand in the square near the Prešeren monument so the pink church is behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: It's an open public square and you can visit at all hours, but check the official site first if festivals or events are planned.
card.challenge: Get the statue on a gridline with the church facade right behind it, then wait for a gap in the bridge crowd and snap it before the next group wanders in.
card.good_to_know: The church is baroque and dates from the 17th century. The statue went up in 1905, designed by Ivan Zajec, with a pedestal by Max Fabiani. The square got its round shape in 1987-88 and has been closed to ordinary motor traffic since 2007, so you can line up your photo without worrying about cars.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje) and face back toward Prešeren Square. The statue of France Prešeren sits in the middle distance, with the pink Franciscan Church filling the background.

card.hook: This isn't a postcard spot, and that's the fun of it. It's a real, busy arrival scene, with people pulling suitcases past a bronze horse and rider.
card.stand_here: Walk east to Trg Osvobodilne fronte, the square in front of the station, with the General Maister monument park alongside. Face the station's front facade and main entrance.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x if the square is busy or you're close to the facade. Use 1x for a natural view, then zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the monument or the entrance details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the building's vertical edges up with them so the walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Go in daylight, ideally when the square is quieter and the light is soft. Early morning may be calmer, though that depends on the day and on the building works.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the open forecourt outside the main entrance (Trg Osvobodilne fronte 7) with the station building behind you. Use the front camera, hold it a little low and try 0.5x to fit more of the building over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to step back on the open forecourt outside the entrance until the whole station front fits, while you stand in front of the entrance.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay off the tracks, shunting areas and railway land, and keep well back from the platform edge. The station is a working building under reconstruction, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the bronze horse and rider, the station and one passing pedestrian all in the same frame, and see if the pedestrian gives your photo a sense of scale.
card.good_to_know: The station was completed on 18 April 1848, a year before the Vienna–Trieste Southern Railway reached Ljubljana. Marko Mušič renovated it in 1980. Nearby is a small James Joyce monument by Jakov Brdar, put up in 2003, because Joyce spent a night here in 1904 after wrongly thinking he'd reached Trieste. Rebuilding began in autumn 2024 and is planned to finish in 2026, so the facade may be partly behind hoardings or fencing. If it is, shoot the monument and the square with the building behind, and take close shots of details instead.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Walk east to Trg Osvobodilne fronte, the square in front of the station, with the General Maister monument park alongside. Face the station's front facade and main entrance.

card.hook: Here's an opinion: the best funicular photo is taken before you board it. The cabin windows are dirty, but the little station and the track climbing the wooded hill make a lovely clean shape from outside.
card.stand_here: Stand in Krekov trg, on the east side, by the lower funicular station (Krekov trg 4). Face the station so the track climbs the wooded hill ahead of you, with a bit of the square in front.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get the station and the track together. Try 0.5x if you want more of the square around you, and 2x or more to pick out the line climbing the hill.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the track up with one of them so it doesn't look tilted, then tap the station and slide the brightness down a touch so the sky doesn't wash out the hillside.
card.best_time: Go in daylight, when the hillside and the station are clearly lit. Early in the day the square is likely to be quieter, and since people stroll through, take a few frames.
card.selfie_here: Try the streets below the funicular on the Old Town side near Krekov trg, looking back up toward the castle. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x, and keep the castle hill over your shoulder. It won't show the funicular behind you, but the view back up is worth a frame or two.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the square a few steps back from the station, while you stand in front of it, so the whole lower station fits in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: The funicular is a ticketed ride and its hours and fares vary, so check the official site before you go. Photographing it from the square needs no ticket.
card.challenge: Get the track running perfectly along a gridline with a strip of square at the bottom, and no strangers walking through. Good luck with that last bit!
card.good_to_know: The funicular opened on 28 December 2006 and was designed as part of the castle's renovation. The idea is much older, though: in 1897 the then mayor, Ivan Hribar, wrote to the Austro-Hungarian authorities to ask for a lift up to the castle. The ride takes about a minute.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Krekov trg, on the east side, by the lower funicular station (Krekov trg 4). Face the station so the track climbs the wooded hill ahead of you, with a bit of the square in front.

selfie_spots.why: The view back up at the castle from the funicular and the streets below is worth a frame or two on the way. This is the only page-named option I found, and it does not clearly show the funicular itself behind you.

card.hook: Cheese, flowers and a pile of fruit, with a long curved Plečnik hall lined up behind them like a film set. This is a working market, so the best photos are the busy, colourful ones.
card.stand_here: Stand in Vodnikov trg, the open-air market area on the square beside the arcades. Face the stalls so the Plečnik halls run along the riverside behind them. The main market hall is to the north.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the stalls and the street scene. Go to 0.5x when you want the whole arcade in one shot. Use 2x or more (depends on your phone) for close-ups of produce, flowers and cheese, so you don't crowd the stallholders.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the stall you want sharp, then slide it a touch darker so bright flowers and fruit keep their colour.
card.best_time: Before 10 am is best, when the square is quieter and the tour groups haven't arrived yet. The market trades daily except Sundays, but check the official site for current days and times.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside the Valentin Vodnik statue in the market area on Vodnikov trg, with the stalls behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if you want more of the market in the frame, and hold the phone a little higher.

card.challenge: Find the most colourful stall, put it in the foreground, and see if you can get the arcade behind it with the gridlines keeping the colonnade nice and level.
card.good_to_know: Jože Plečnik designed the long, curved market hall in the 1930s, and it was built in the early 1940s. Vodnikov trg has been an outdoor market since the 1895 earthquake cleared the buildings that stood there. Since August 2021 the market has been part of Plečnik's legacy on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

card.hook: Picture Ljubljana in 1933: a brand-new 70-metre tower pops up among the Baroque bell towers, and some locals are NOT happy about it. Today Nebotičnik is one of the city's best-loved landmarks.
card.stand_here: The phone icon sits on Nebotičnik itself, so don't stop there. Walk back across the street until the whole tower fits, then face it and tilt your phone up just a little. Right by the entrance you'll only get the lower floors and the stonework.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x from across the street for the whole tower. If you're close and need the full height, try zoom 0.5x. Then zoom 2x or 5x for the round colonnade on top or the sculpture on the side (higher zooms depend on your phone).
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the sides of the tower up with the vertical lines so it doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Soft daylight in the morning or late afternoon is kind to the stonework. After sunset, switch on night mode and catch the tower against a darkening sky.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera and step back across the street so the tower can fit behind you. Try zoom 0.5x, hold the phone a bit lower and tilt it up, and keep the tower over your shoulder. Take a few, because the top floors are easy to cut off.
card.rules_and_safety: The outside is easy to photograph from the street. The café, bar and observation deck are on the top floors, so check the official site before you go up.
card.challenge: Spot the four-metre woman sculpture on the side façade, level with the sixth floor, and get a detail shot of her without tipping your phone sideways.
card.good_to_know: Nebotičnik means 'the Skyscraper'. It has thirteen storeys and stands 70.35 m tall. Architect Vladimir Šubic mixed neoclassical and art-deco styles, and it opened on 21 February 1933 as the tallest building in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia.

card.hook: Yes, the church really is that pink, and it's on purpose. It's the one building on Prešeren Square that's hard to lose in a crowd.
card.stand_here: Head for Prešernov trg and stand at the southern end of the square. Face north, with the church straight ahead and the granite paving stretching out in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole facade and the paving in one go. Switch to 1x for a calmer, less stretched look. Use 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the statue at the top and the niches above the doors.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, hold your phone upright and level so the towers don't lean, and leave a band of paving at the bottom to lead the eye up the stairs.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning if you can. The square is quiet and the foreground is clear, before the market and café furniture fill it up.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside the Prešeren statue on the Triple Bridge side of the square, front camera on, with the pink church rising behind you. For another backdrop, try the Fishmarket Footbridge (Ribja brv) with the church and Triple Bridge over your shoulder. One guide says most Instagram photos in Ljubljana are taken from there.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Triple Bridge and face back toward the square, while you stand in the square so the whole church is behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: It's a place of worship, so dress and behave respectfully. Photography inside may not be allowed, so check the official site before you go. The view may be blocked at times by construction in front of the church.
card.challenge: Zoom in to 5x and find the copper statue of Our Lady of Loretto at the top, then count the three niches above the main doors.
card.good_to_know: The church was built between 1646 and 1660, and the bell towers followed around 1720. The pink is symbolic of the Franciscan order. It replaced an earlier white finish when the exterior was redesigned in 1858. Since 2008 the church has been protected as a cultural monument of national significance.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for Prešernov trg and stand at the southern end of the square. Face north, with the church straight ahead and the granite paving stretching out in front of you.

card.hook: Two greens, one frame: a green dragon guarding the bridge and a green dome across the river. Ljubljana has made this one easy for you.
card.stand_here: Stand on Zmajski most (the Dragon Bridge) and face south-west across the river. The cathedral's green dome and twin towers sit ahead of you, with one of the bridge's green dragon sculptures close by.
card.zoom: Start at 1x so the dragon, the river and the cathedral all fit. The cathedral is a little way off, so try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to fill the frame with the dome and towers.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines to keep the towers upright and the bridge edge level, then tap the dome and make the picture a touch darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light suits the green dome. Go early if you want fewer people on the bridge.
card.selfie_here: Head to Pogačarjev trg, the square in front of the cathedral, and stand with the cathedral filling the view behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to fit more of the church in, and keep the market stalls out of the corner of your frame.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to shoot from the bridge corner where a green dragon statue sits in the foreground, so the cathedral shows up beyond it.
card.rules_and_safety: The cathedral is a working place of worship, so dress modestly if you go inside and check the official site for visiting arrangements. Photos without flash are generally tolerated inside outside of services, but be discreet and follow any posted signs or staff instructions.
card.challenge: Take one shot with the dragon and one without, then pick the one that feels most balanced and declare a winner.
card.good_to_know: Ljubljana Cathedral is officially the Church of Saint Nicholas. A Gothic church once stood here, and the Baroque building that replaced it was put up between 1701 and 1706 and consecrated on 8 May 1707. The Jesuit architect Andrea Pozzo reworked the plan and added the dome, and the two belfries carry gilded apples.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Zmajski most (the Dragon Bridge) and face south-west across the river. The cathedral's green dome and twin towers sit ahead of you, with one of the bridge's green dragon sculptures close by.

card.hook: Here's a little opinion: don't march straight into Mestni trg. Take the picture from across the river first, where the water gives the old town some depth and the rooflines line up nicely.
card.stand_here: Stand on Tromostovje, the embankment by the Triple Bridge on the Ljubljanica. Face south across the river so the Town Square and the old town rooflines fill your screen.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the full view across the river. Try 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Town Hall and the rooflines, or the castle on a clear day. Use 0.5x only if you want lots of river and sky, because it makes the square look small.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the river along the lower third, then tap the buildings and slide the picture a touch darker if the sky is bright, so the facades keep their colour.
card.best_time: Go at sunrise or sunset for lovely golden light. The square is worth a visit at other times of day too.
card.selfie_here: Walk into Mestni trg and stand beside the Robba Fountain, the spot guides call the square's must-capture backdrop. Use the front camera and frame it so the square and the Town Hall open up behind you over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Triple Bridge and photograph you with the square in view across the river.
card.rules_and_safety: The cobblestones in the square are uneven, so watch your step while you line up the shot. The square and the embankment are open public space, but check the official site first if you plan to go inside any building.
card.challenge: On a clear day, get the castle into your shot without letting it shrink to a dot, then take a few frames and pick the one with nobody walking through it.
card.good_to_know: The fountain in front of the Town Hall is a copy of the Robba Fountain, and the original is kept in the National Gallery. Opposite stands the Krisper House, where Julija Primic, the inspiration of the poet France Prešeren, was born in 1816. The composer Gustav Mahler also lived there in 1881-82.

card.hook: Plot twist: the grand fountain you're about to photograph is a body double, and nobody in the square seems to mind. The three muscular figures still steal the show.
card.stand_here: Stand on Tromostovje, the Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica, and look back toward the square. The fountain is to the south-east, framed across the river with Ljubljana Castle behind it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so you get the river, the fountain and the castle in one shot. Then try zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the three figures and the obelisk across the water.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the white marble figures, then drag the brightness slider down a little so the stone keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Right after sunrise is best. The light on the sculptures is lovely and there are fewer tour groups. Light can vary, so try morning and late afternoon if you can.
card.selfie_here: Head into Mestni trg, in front of the Town Hall, and pose beside the fountain's basin and statues. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x to fit more in, and keep the fountain over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by in Mestni trg to frame you with the fountain in front and St Nicholas Cathedral rising behind it.
card.rules_and_safety: The cobblestones around the square are uneven, so wear comfortable shoes. Please don't climb on the fountain, because the figures are fragile.
card.challenge: Take three shots in a row and see if you can get one with nobody walking through the frame. Good luck!
card.good_to_know: Francesco Robba, an Italian sculptor, made the original in 1751. The three figures with dolphins and water jugs came to be read as the river gods of the Sava, Krka and Ljubljanica. The fountain in the square is a replica from 2006, and the restored original has been in the National Gallery of Slovenia since 2008.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Tromostovje, the Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica, and look back toward the square. The fountain is to the south-east, framed across the river with Ljubljana Castle behind it.

card.hook: The Satyr on Butchers' Bridge looks properly startled, and you'll probably feel the same when you realise this short footbridge is packed with bronze characters.
card.stand_here: Stand right on the deck of Butchers' Bridge, at the phone icon on the map, next to the bronze sculptures and the padlocked railings. Face whichever sculpture or row of padlocks you like best and fill the frame with it.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the sculptures and padlocks. Try 2x if your phone has it to pick out a single figure, then switch to 0.5x for a wide shot along the whole deck.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the bronze, then slide the brightness down a little so the metal keeps its detail, and turn on gridlines to put your figure on a third.
card.best_time: Late afternoon or around sunset is lovely, when low light falls on the bronze and the glass.
card.selfie_here: Try the Petkovškovo embankment (Petkovškovo nabrežje) across the water from the bridge, near the bench. Use the front camera at 0.5x with the bridge over your shoulder. It's the closest spot we know with the bridge in view, but it's a best guess rather than a confirmed selfie spot, so check how it looks before you settle in.
card.ask_someone: Stand on the Petkovškovo bank facing the bridge across the river, and ask a passer-by on the same bank to frame you with the whole bridge behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Watch your step on the glass walkway, which can be slippery when wet, and mind other visitors who stop to look at the sculptures.
card.challenge: Hunt down the little frogs and shellfish along the top of the fence and get one of them sharp in your shot.
card.good_to_know: The bridge opened on 10 July 2010 and was designed by Jurij Kobe. It's about 33 metres long and 17.3 metres wide, and the bronze sculptures are by Jakov Brdar. Jože Plečnik had imagined a much grander, covered bridge on this spot in the 1930s, but it was never built.

card.hook: Most people march straight into the courtyard, but the better picture is outside, where two tall stone walls are waiting to frame you. Križevniška soteska is a narrow passage that does half your composing for you.
card.stand_here: Stand in Križevniška soteska, the stone-walled passage along the outer walls of Križanke. From French Revolution Square, the theatre outline lies to the west, about 1 minute on foot. Face towards Zoisova cesta so the passage runs away from you. Confirm the exact spot when you get there.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit both walls and the passage in one shot. Then try 1x for a more natural look at the stonework, and 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for stone texture or the far end of the passage.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line a vertical grid line up with a wall edge, so the walls stand straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Go for soft daylight, either morning or late afternoon, when the stone looks good and the passage has less harsh contrast. Check the event schedule first, because the area can be closed for concerts.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the path beside the old monastery walls with the walls behind you, and use the front camera. Try zoom 0.5x if your front camera has it, and hold the phone a bit lower so the stone rises up over your shoulder. If you'd rather be inside, the main courtyard has arches and stonework that make a good backdrop.
card.rules_and_safety: Križanke can be closed during events and concerts, so check the official site before you go and respect any closures.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot and one close shot of the same wall, and see which one makes the passage look longer.
card.good_to_know: Building is believed to have started in 1228, when this was a monastery of the Teutonic Knights. The church was rebuilt in Baroque style in 1714-15 by the Venetian architect Domenico Rossi. In the early 1950s the city asked Jože Plečnik to turn the empty buildings into a festival venue, and his work was finished in 1956.

card.hook: Tragedy and Comedy have been standing in their niches here for over a century, and neither one looks like they're leaving. They're easy to find, too, because the Opera House sits between the Slovenian Parliament and the National Museum and National Gallery.
card.stand_here: Stand in front of the main facade on the Župančičeva street side (the address is Župančičeva 1) and face the building. From here the whole columned front fits into one picture.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x if you're close, so every column squeezes in. Step back and use 1x for a more natural look. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) for the tympanum and the Tragedy and Comedy statues.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and line the columns up with the vertical lines so the building doesn't lean, then keep the entrance in the middle.
card.best_time: Come at dusk, when the portico is lit. Lighting can vary, so check on the day.
card.selfie_here: Try the stone pedestals in front of the building, beside the busts of Anton Verovšek and Ignacij Borštnik. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the columns and tympanum over your shoulder. For a quieter angle, stand by the Julij Betetto sculpture on the side of the building along Cankarjeva street.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos inside usually depend on the venue's rules, so ask staff if you go to a performance.
card.challenge: Take one big straight-on shot of the whole front, then one close-up of Tragedy or Comedy, and decide which one has the better poses.
card.good_to_know: The Opera House was first called the Provincial Theatre. Czech architects Jan Vladimír Hráský and Anton Hruby built it between 1890 and 1892 in the Neo-Renaissance style. Until the German Theatre opened in 1911 it staged shows in both Slovene and German, and after that only in Slovene. The Tragedy and Comedy statues are by the sculptor Alojz Gangl.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in front of the main facade on the Župančičeva street side (the address is Župančičeva 1) and face the building. From here the whole columned front fits into one picture.

card.hook: Quick plot twist: the Tivoli "castle" you want is really a mansion at the bottom of a park, not the big one on the hill in the Old Town. Its secret weapon is a long tree-lined avenue that points straight at it.
card.stand_here: Stand on Jakopičevo sprehajališče (the Jakopič Promenade), at its lower end, and face uphill along the avenue. The mansion will be straight ahead, to the west.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to catch the whole avenue with the mansion at the end. Then try zoom 2x or higher (depends on your phone) for a tighter shot with the trees close around the building. If a photo exhibition is on, zoom 0.5x lets you pull a panel into the foreground.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, centre yourself on the avenue and keep the phone upright, then tap the mansion and drag the brightness down a touch if the sky is bright.
card.best_time: Mornings are quieter and moodier, so that's your best bet for an avenue without crowds. Afternoons get busier.
card.selfie_here: Walk up to the foot of the stairs and pose beside one of the cast-iron dogs, so the mansion fills the background. Or use the small lawn next to the Dancing Couple statue: face away from the mansion with your front camera so it sits behind you, and try zoom 0.5x to fit more in. Guides mention these spots, so check the dogs and statue are still there.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the lower end of the promenade and aim up the avenue while you stand at the foot of the stairs, with the whole mansion rising above you.
card.rules_and_safety: After rain or snow, wear proper shoes, because the unpaved side paths in the park can get muddy. The gallery inside may be ticketed, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Find all four cast-iron dogs out front, then get one of them sitting in the foreground with the mansion right behind it.
card.good_to_know: The current building dates from the 17th century and stands on the ruins of an earlier Renaissance castle. It began as a Jesuit property, then became the bishop's summer residence. In 1852 Marshal Joseph Radetzky renovated it in the Neoclassical style, and since 1967 it has housed the International Centre of Graphic Arts.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Jakopičevo sprehajališče (the Jakopič Promenade), at its lower end, and face uphill along the avenue. The mansion will be straight ahead, to the west.

card.hook: Picture a neat Baroque front with a clock tower, and a fountain parked right in front of it like it knows it's being photographed. That's the Rotovž, Ljubljana's Town Hall, and you get building and street life in one frame.
card.stand_here: Stand in the middle of Mestni trg (Town Square) and face the Town Hall's north façade. The Robba fountain will be in front of the building, with the Cathedral and castle hill behind it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole façade, clock tower and fountain into this tight square. Then try 1x for a more natural look with less stretching at the edges. If your phone has 2x or 5x, use it for the clock tower or the fountain details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn the phone upright, switch on gridlines to keep the building's edges straight, and put the fountain low in the frame with the façade above it.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, when the sun rises behind the castle. The square is largely in shade in the afternoons.
card.selfie_here: Stand by the Robba fountain with the Town Hall rising behind you, use the front camera at 0.5x, and keep the building over your shoulder. For a second option, try under the arcades in the inner courtyard (Mestna hiša), with the arches around you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back across the open square in front of the building so the façade and clock tower fit, while you stand by the fountain.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is generally allowed in public areas of the Town Hall, but it can differ for exhibitions and ceremonial rooms, so follow posted signs or staff instructions. It's a working building, so events or weddings can sometimes block the front view.
card.challenge: Take one shot with the fountain empty and one with people milling around it, then pick the winner later.
card.good_to_know: The first building here was Gothic, dated 1484. Between 1717 and 1719 it was renovated in a Venetian-inspired Baroque style, which gave it the gable front, the loggia and the three-part staircase you see today. The fountain outside is a replica of Francesco Robba's work, and the original, finished in 1751, is kept in the National Gallery.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in the middle of Mestni trg (Town Square) and face the Town Hall's north façade. The Robba fountain will be in front of the building, with the Cathedral and castle hill behind it.

card.hook: A dark bronze poet, a muse perched above him and a big pink church behind them: it looks like the church was painted to match your photo. This is Slovenia's national poet, and the setting does most of the work for you.
card.stand_here: Stand at the square-side end of the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje), about 70 m from the Prešeren Monument. The statue is to the north of you, so face north with the river Ljubljanica running across your frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the classic view of the poet with the church behind him. Tap 2x to bring the church closer and pick out the poet and the muse. Save zoom 0.5x for when you're down in the square and want the whole monument and the buildings around it in one shot.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the bronze poet, then slide the brightness down a touch so the pink church and the sky don't wash out.
card.best_time: Sunset or golden hour is the winner, when the pink church glows. Midday, event days and 8 February (Prešeren Day) get busy, so go early or later in the day for a clearer view of the statue.
card.selfie_here: Climb up to the steps around the statue and face toward Julija's window. Visitors like to copy the poet's gaze, so use the front camera, hold it a bit higher, and let the bronze poet be your backdrop. For a playful foreground, try the sun-shaped fountain in the middle of the square instead, with the statue nearby.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone standing on the Triple Bridge to frame the square while you stand by the statue, so you both fit in the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: An older guide says sitting on the statue's steps was once forbidden, so check for signs on the day. Selfies can be tricky in the crowds, so early or late is easier.
card.challenge: Can you place the poet's head so the church roofline doesn't grow out of it?
card.good_to_know: The poet is France Prešeren, and he holds a book that stands for his Poems. The figure is 3.5 metres high and the whole monument is 9.6 metres. It was unveiled on 10 September 1905 in front of more than 20,000 people. Look at the pedestal too: two bronze reliefs show scenes from his poems.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the square-side end of the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje), about 70 m from the Prešeren Monument. The statue is to the north of you, so face north with the river Ljubljanica running across your frame.

card.hook: Picture a bridge so smelly that an Emperor paid to move the butchers off it. That's the Cobblers' Bridge, and today the only thing you'll smell is the river air.
card.stand_here: Stand on Ribja brv, the neighbouring footbridge, and face back toward the Cobblers' Bridge. The bridge, the colourful riverside houses and the castle all fit in one frame from there.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the bridge, the houses and the castle together. If it's busy and you can't step back, tap 0.5x. Use zoom 2x to pick out the castle or the lamp pillars.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the bright sky or the castle, then drag the slider to make the picture a little darker so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Sunday flea-market hours and evenings with buskers are the busiest, so skip them if you want fewer people on the bridge. If you do stay for the evening, try night mode and rest your phone against the railing to keep the shot steady.
card.selfie_here: Try the southern end of the bridge, with the castle on the hill behind you, or stand on the bridge deck between the rows of columns, which frame the castle and river. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the castle over your shoulder. No guide names an exact selfie spot, so have a quick look around on the day.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to shoot from the Cankarjevo nabrežje embankment at the river's edge, so the whole span shows behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The bridge is pedestrian-only and open to the public.
card.challenge: Find a lamp pillar and use it as a foreground frame, with the castle peeking out behind it.
card.good_to_know: There has been a bridge here since at least the 13th century. It began as a wooden bridge with butchers' stalls, and shoemakers took over the booths after the smell got too much, which is how it got its name. The current stone bridge was designed by Jože Plečnik in 1931 and became part of his UNESCO World Heritage listing in 2021.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Ribja brv, the neighbouring footbridge, and face back toward the Cobblers' Bridge. The bridge, the colourful riverside houses and the castle all fit in one frame from there.
